Subject: Segmented discount scenarios and migration runbook

Tom / team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion I pulled together two concrete paths to get EllipticOps to parity on unit economics while preserving go-live SLAs and minimizing ops lift: a staged-credit path tied to actual usage and a bundled-commit path with a one-time onboarding credit.

Key differences at a glance:
- Staged-credit (recommended for velocity): 3-month ramp of credits that redeem against tokens; credits release based on weekly traffic thresholds so you don’t overcommit.
- Bundled-commit (recommended for pricing predictability): 12-month term with a 15% list discount + onboarding credit that covers migration egress and early support.

Operational notes: both paths include a technical runbook for migration steps, a SKU mapping table for model parity, and a fallback window where we hold a small buffer of dedicated capacity for the first 30 days. I’ve attached the runbook and a working cost model for your review.

Ask: can you confirm which commercial framing your procurement team prefers (staged credits vs bundled commit)? If we get a preference today I can loop legal and prepare a short term sheet for signature next week.

Attachments: Redwood_Segmented_Discount_Runbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.1 MB); ELP-cost-model-v2.xlsx (Excel, 220 KB)

Thanks,

3) We’ll need a clearer breakdown of who owns egress costs during the migration week — can you call out what the onboarding credit covers?

Tom —

Thanks, good questions. Short answers first, then I pasted the updated runbook excerpt below. Full files are attached and I also pushed a read-only folder to your team (link in metadata).

1) Credits & spikes: Credits in the staged plan are not retroactive by default, but we propose a weekly reconciliation that allows you to carry forward up to 20% of unused credits for the subsequent week within the 3-month window — that protects bursty workloads.

2) Bundled-commit discount structure: Base 15% off list at the base consumption tier; we include a tiered uplift (20% at >2.5x baseline monthly usage, 25% at >4x) — the idea is to reward scale while keeping predictable unit pricing.

3) Onboarding credit coverage: the onboarding credit (applies to the bundled path) is scoped to egress costs for the initial data extract (one-time), two weeks of dedicated-support hours for migration verification, and up to $10k of secure transfer expenses (if using our dedicated transfer tooling). It does NOT cover third-party ETL vendor fees.

Runbook excerpt (snippet):
- Prework (network & security): exchange IP allowlist, confirm KMS ACLs, confirm audit log retention settings.
- Pilot (week 0): send a 1TB sample export, validate model parity on 50k inference calls, run latency profiles during peak window.
- Cutover (week 1): dual-write for 48 hours -> monitor 99th percentile token latency and error budget -> if >1.5x error rate, trigger rollback plan A.
- Rollback plan A: switch writes back to incumbent for 24 hours, flush KV cache, and use dedicated warmed nodes for validation.

Commercial ask: if procurement likes staged credits we’ll need a signed LOI for a 3-month credit pool so we can reserve burst capacity. If bundled-commit is preferred, I’ll draft the term sheet and schedule a 30-minute legal/finance sync.

Attachments: Redwood_Segmented_Discount_Runbook_v1.pdf; ELP-cost-model-v2.xlsx

Quick technical add:

- We can support the staged-credit flow with a soft rollback window that preserves KV cache snapshots for the first 72 hours post-cutover; that reduces cold-cache latency significantly and lowers the risk of user-impact during the ramp.
- I recommend adjusting the credit-release schedule to be cadence-based (week 0: 40%, week 1: 30%, week 2+: weekly 10% increments) rather than strictly traffic-thresholded. The cadence approach is easier to reconcile in finance systems and avoids disputes over spikes.
- On the egress scope: if EllipticOps wants us to shoulder a portion of third-party ETL costs, we can do so but it needs to be an explicit line-item in the term sheet (we can offer up to $5k toward vetted ETL tooling).

Naomi / Marissa: if you want I can draft the term-sheet bullet points and a one-pager checklist for operations to sign off during the pilot.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
